# Compass Anti-Patterns — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Compass Anti-Patterns. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-23 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] When reviewing a collection in Compass, unnecessary indexes and bloated documents are legitimate investigation targets. MongoDB documents their disk-space, write-cost, and query-performance consequences; the presence of an index or a large document alone does not establish that it is unnecessary or bloated. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] MongoDB's schema anti-pattern catalogue covers unbounded arrays, excessive collection counts, unnecessary indexes, bloated documents, and excessive $lookup operations. Independent research catalogues related MongoDB smells; its literature synthesis is corroborating context, not an independent measurement of Compass detection coverage. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns.md ; https://susi.usi.ch/usi/documents/329705 — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns.md · keywords: Compass Anti-Patterns · also: https://susi.usi.ch/documents/329705/files/Nagy_Lanza_2024_IEEE_SANER.pdf
- [statement] Allowing an embedded array to grow without a bound can exhaust document-size limits and impose resource costs. MongoDB documents a 16MB BSON document size limit and says an unbounded array can strain application resources and decrease index performance. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns/unbounded-arrays.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns/unbounded-arrays.md · keywords: Compass Anti-Patterns · also: https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol18/p4804-carey.pdf
- [statement] An anti-pattern warning does not justify banning arrays. MongoDB says arrays let you embed data that is accessed together, and recommends subsetting and referencing to bound arrays rather than embedding entire datasets. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns/unbounded-arrays.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns/unbounded-arrays.md · keywords: Compass Anti-Patterns · also: https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol18/p4804-carey.pdf
- [statement] COMPASS-9163 reports that importing a numeric embedding array of 251 elements triggers a large-array warning. Its report distinguishes import warning logic from schema insight logic. This establishes a reported warning mismatch, not universal behavior across Compass releases. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-19) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/COMPASS-9163
- [statement] Compass schema analysis works on a sample: it samples 1,000 documents from a collection using the $sample operator, and sample results tend to be similar to, but are not guaranteed to match, results for the entire data set. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/compass/sampling.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/compass/sampling.md · keywords: Compass Anti-Patterns · also: https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-compass-schema-analysis/view
- [statement] An embedded history that grows without a bound is a design risk even when it initially looks convenient in Compass. Growing arrays can strain resources and eventually exceed document limits; bounded subsets or separately stored related records can address the growth. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns/unbounded-arrays.md · keywords: Compass Anti-Patterns · also: https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol18/p4804-carey.pdf

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Fixing unbounded arrays involves trade-offs: a bounded subset duplicates data and makes updates more expensive, while external references can require additional queries and latency. Select the remedy for the workload rather than treating every join as a design error. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns/unbounded-arrays.md · keywords: Compass Anti-Patterns · also: https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol18/p4804-carey.pdf
- [statement] Increasing schema-analysis coverage has a cost: larger samples or whole-collection inspection require more time and processing. Use query filters to investigate relevant document segments rather than assuming one broad sample answers every question. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/compass/sampling.md · keywords: Compass Anti-Patterns · also: https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-compass-schema-analysis/view

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Replacing embedded objects with an ever-growing array of their IDs does not necessarily remove unbounded growth. The document-database design paper explicitly warns about customer documents that retain every order reference; assess the cardinality and growth of references as well as embedded objects. (medium confidence) — https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol18/p4804-carey.pdf · keywords: Compass Anti-Patterns · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns/unbounded-arrays.md
- [statement] Unnecessary indexes and bloated documents deserve explicit review: MongoDB documents that unnecessary indexes consume additional disk space and can degrade write performance, and that bloated (excessively large) documents can degrade the performance of the most common queries, in part because the working set may no longer fit in RAM. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns/bloated-documents.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns.md · keywords: Compass Anti-Patterns · also: https://susi.usi.ch/documents/329705/files/Nagy_Lanza_2024_IEEE_SANER.pdf
- [statement] Compass sampling documentation describes a 1,000-document $sample aggregation over a collection or query-selected subset. Treating such a sample as proof that no rare schema defect exists is an inference the evidence does not support. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/compass/sampling.md
- [statement] Using data values such as dates as field names can make range queries awkward and prevent straightforward secondary indexing. The document-database design paper recommends explicit fields for those values; this is an additional manual review check, not a documented Compass detector. (low confidence) — https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol18/p4804-carey.pdf
